notes: Error basis: a 80% interval needs at least 19 errors per horizon to be an interior quantile rather than the observed min/max, and this series has fewer (h1: 11, h2: 11, h3: 11), so all 33 errors are pooled across horizons. Pooling understates uncertainty at the far horizon and overstates it at the near one, but it is the honest choice at this sample size.
Calibration is based on 33 out-of-sample error(s), below the 40 at which a two-sided 95% conformal interval first becomes attainable. Treat the bounds as indicative rather than guaranteed.

factors.label: Validation error
factors.explanation: Historical forecast error is high. Across walk-forward validation the forecast was off by 46.8% of actual volume on average (forecasting zero every period would score 100%).

factors.label: Fold-to-fold consistency
factors.explanation: Accuracy varied between 11.1% and 68.3% WAPE across validation folds. The worst window was 6.2x the error of the best, so performance in any single future window is hard to anticipate.

factors.label: History available
factors.explanation: 48 monthly periods supported 11 independent validation folds. That is at or near the 12-fold design target, so the error estimate rests on a reasonable amount of evidence.

factors.label: Input data quality
factors.explanation: Every one of the 48 modelled periods contains real recorded transactions, and the input needed little correction.

factors.label: Uncertainty calibration
factors.explanation: The 80% interval actually contained the outcome 67% of the time across 21 out-of-sample checks (-13.3pp against its 80% target). Calibration rests on a limited number of out-of-sample errors, so the stated levels are indicative rather than guaranteed.

factors.label: Model selection strength
factors.explanation: Simple Exponential Smoothing (46.82% WAPE) beat Naive (51.40%) by 4.58pp, which is 0.27x the 17.15pp fold-to-fold variation. The margin is smaller than the noise between folds, so several models perform similarly here and the ranking could change on different data.

factors.label: Prediction interval width
factors.explanation: The 80% prediction range is about 2.2 times the size of the forecast itself. That is a wide range — the forecast is best used as a rough planning estimate. Width follows from the accuracy and consistency measured above, so it is shown here as context rather than counted again in the score.

warnings: Prediction interval calibration is limited by the amount of historical validation data available.
The 95% interval exceeds what the available validation history can support and will understate true uncertainty.
reliability.interpretation: Forecast reliability is a 0-100 rating of how much evidence supports this forecast — its measured accuracy, how consistent that accuracy is over time, how much history it rests on, the quality of the input data, and whether its uncertainty range is calibrated. It is NOT a probability that the forecast is correct, and it should not be read as one. For the likely range of outcomes, use the prediction interval.

model_explanation.reason: Simple Exponential Smoothing achieved the lowest validated error for Company Total (46.82% WAPE across 11 leakage-safe walk-forward folds).
model_explanation.strength_reason: Simple Exponential Smoothing ranked first, but its 4.58pp advantage over Naive is smaller than the 17.15pp variation between validation folds. Several models performed similarly here, and the ranking could change on different data.

trend.explanation: Revenue rose over the observed periods, by about 0.8% of the series average per period (trend strength 0.21).

seasonality.explanation: Only a weak repeating seasonal pattern was measured over a 12-month cycle (strength 0.20). Seasonal models therefore have little structure to exploit here.

volatility.explanation: Period-to-period revenue is moderately variable (coefficient of variation 0.61). This level of variability puts a practical floor under achievable forecast error.

data_quality.explanation: Good — 48 monthly observations from 392 transactions, with complete period coverage.

a 95% level that exceeds what the available validation history supports
